title: Recording: Listen To What The Man Said, My Carnival, Crossroads by Wings | 1975
content:
Sea-Saint Recording Studio, New Orleans
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Alan O’Duffy, Ken Laxton, Roberta Grace

Wings worked on three songs for the Venus And Mars album on 31 January 1975.

The first was ‘Listen To What The Man Said’. It featured Paul McCartney on electric piano, Jimmy McCulloch on electric guitar, Denny Laine on bongos, and Joe English on drums. McCartney then overdubbed a bass guitar part before setting the track aside.

Wings then jammed for a while, and played a piece listed in the session notes as ‘Scottish Jingle’, another titled ‘CLematis’, and a piece written by Linda McCartney titled ‘New Orleans’.

They then worked on a new Paul McCartney piece initially known as ‘Goin’ To New Orleans’, but later retitled ‘My Carnival’. Wings returned to it on 12 February, but it remained unreleased until 1985 when McCartney issued it as the b-side of the ‘Spies Like Us’ single.

Wings’ jamming eventually resulted in a version of the theme of UK soap opera ‘Crossroads’, which became the closing song on Venus And Mars.

It’s a joke! It’s after ‘Lonely Old People’, you see. They are sitting there in the park, saying, ‘Nobody asked us to play’. It’s a poignant moment. Then there’s a little break and then ‘Crossroads’ starts up. It’s lonely old people. It’s just the kind of thing that lonely old people watch. It could just as easily have been Coronation Street, but we knew the chords to ‘Crossroads’. I just thought that it would be nice to do it.
Paul McCartney
New Orleans press conference, 1975

The 23-piece orchestra for ‘Crossroads’ was overdubbed on 10 March at Sunset Sound Recorders in Los Angeles. The song was completed later in the month at Wally Heider Studios in LA.
